newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-PARMA TURN SEASON AROUND WITH TWO TITANIC VICTORIES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARMA TURN SEASON AROUND WITH TWO TITANIC VICTORIES.

text.p: Consecutive wins against the big two sides of Italian soccer, Juventus and AC Milan, have turned around a hitherto disappointing season for normally competitive Parma.
On Sunday, Parma did themselves and all other serie A title aspirants a big favour by defeating league leaders and European champions Juventus 1-0.
That win, on the first fixture day of 1997, followed an equally impressive 1-0 win away to Milan on the last day of 1996.
Four weeks ago, Parma were just above the relegation zone and new coach Carlo Ancelotti seemed destined for imminent unemployment.

Seven points picked up against Juventus, Milan and second-placed Vicenza, with whom Parma drew late last year, have changed all that, leaving Ancelotti's side in mid-table, eight points behind Juventus.
Parma President Stefano Tanzi has no doubts his side have left the worse behind them.

"At last we've seen the real team, a side that battles and never gives up," he said after Sunday's victory. "The squad is solid and united and I think we can aim for second place in the title race, which this year gets you into the Champions' League."

Good results in their last three outings represent long overdue returns for a summer of heavy investment by Parma, one of the most successful Italian club sides of the 1990s and winners of the UEFA and Cup Winners' Cups.
Former coach Nevio Scala, the man who masterminded their rise from Division 2 to the top of Europe, was off-loaded in favour of Ancelotti, a younger manager.
Parma splashed out an estimated $35 million on new talent including striker Enrico Chiesa, Argentine striker Hernan Crespo, French defender Lilian Thuram and Brazilian defender Ze Maria.
The new-look Parma started the season badly however with immediate elimination from the Italian Cup by second division Pescara and from the UEFA Cup by Portuguese side Vitoria Guimaraes.
Subsequent league defeats by Lazio, Perugia, Inter and Udinese prompted widespread speculation in early December that the dismissal of Ancelotti would be announced within days.
Furthermore, the sale of top player Gianfranco Zola to English premier league Chelsea in November did little for dressing room morale or for Ancelotti's popularity with some of Parma's fans.
Although Tanzi repeatedly said he did not intend to sack his coach, these two recent big wins have nonetheless taken a great deal of pressure off Ancelotti.

"It's been a difficult period for us all when we have had to put up with all sorts of problems, dressing room tensions, people rowing against us and for us, in short a real mess," a relieved Ancelotti said on Sunday.
"But just let me enjoy this win now...now that we've finally found the right determination and commitment, now that we've learned to fight for 90 minutes."
The 37-year-old coach, a former AS Roma and Milan player, began his managerial career last season with then-second division Reggiana, following a period as assistant to Italy coach Arrigo Sacchi.
As with Parma this season, Reggiana under Ancelotti got off to a poor start only to recover. They ended the season by winning promotion to serie A.
Asked on Sunday if he intended a repeat of that turnaround with Parma he joked: "Problem is, here I have to win the championship title."
